feature: A video shows the Library in its dock, folded
summary: Open a recording and the Library header now sits folded at the foot of the dock, so your clips are one click away without going to View > Library. Pictures still keep the Library out until you ask for it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/video-library-folded-walk.json.

try.do: Open any screen recording (or File > New Video).
Look at the foot of the right panel: LIBRARY Media, folded.
Drag the recording's tile onto a track.
Choose View > Library to turn the shelf off in this video, and again to bring it back.
Open a picture: no Library until View > Library.

evaluate: Would a Premiere editor find their bin where the folded LIBRARY header sits?
Is one folded row at the foot of a recording's dock worth it, or does it feel like clutter?
When you open it, is the shelf tall enough for your clips without taking too much room from Transitions?
Once you have opened or folded the Library, does it stay the way you left it?
rough: Opened, the shelf takes about 40 per cent of the panel and squeezes Transitions to one row of tiles; the mock caps the opened Library at 118 px so it does not split the column (video.html #gLibrary). Covered by on-a-video-captions-and-transitions-sit-where-th, which already owns the Library pane squeezing a video's panel.

The Library now starts folded everywhere until you open it once. In a picture or design that only shows when the shelf is turned on from the Sections list, because View > Library and every command that fills the shelf open it as they reveal it.
Turning the shelf off in a video is remembered for videos only and never touches pictures or design, and starting a new video no longer turns the Library on for design work after it.
